subject: FastByte prepay bridge: proposal for credit vesting & ramp minimums
messages:
From: Zoe Park <zoe@fastbyte.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick ask — startup prepay + credits structure

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost profile looked great. Our exec team asked me to get a concrete prepay proposal so we can decide between two vendors by the end of November.

We’re an early-stage infra startup (Series A, ~30 engineers). Our ask: a 12–24 month prepay option that gives us predictable unit economics during a fast-growth period. Two things that matter to us:
- Front-loaded credits to help during initial growth and spike months
- Lower committed minimums in months 1–3 (we’ll ramp usage quickly but want some buffer)

Can Redwood do a hybrid structure that mixes a shorter locked prepay with a small top-up option later? Also send any terms you typically include for startups (SLA, data retention, credits vesting).

Appreciate it — can we get something by end of week?

— Zoe
Zoe Park
Head of Platform
FastByte, Inc.

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Zoe Park <zoe@fastbyte.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick ask — startup prepay + credits structure

Hi Zoe — thanks for the clear brief and timeline.

Short answer: yes. We commonly structure startup prepay deals with a combination of an upfront committed term and a small optional top-up window; we also offer an "earn-back" credit pool that vests as usage grows. I attached a one-page ramp schedule and a sample credit vesting table (see FastByte_RAMP_Schedule_v3.xlsx).

High-level proposal (initial):
- Base term: 12 months prepay at $120k total (covers base usage); treated as a single upfront charge.
- Credits: $40k in platform credits front-loaded at contract start. Credits are applied before overage bills; unspent credits expire after 12 months unless earn-back conditions met.
- Ramp minimums: stair-step minimums for months 1–3 to lower initial burden (month1: 25% of monthly run-rate; month2: 50%; month3: 75%; month4+: 100%).
- Earn-back credits: up to $15k additional credits that vest monthly if month-over-month usage growth >= 15% (vesting rate: 1/6 per qualifying month).
- Optional top-up: a 12-month extension window (months 13–24) where FastByte can elect to prepay an additional amount at a pre-agreed discount to preserve pricing predictability.

Discounts & commercials: base prepay receives a 18% term discount off list pricing; enrolled SLAs (99.9% uptime) can add an incremental 2% rebate if target met.

Open items we need from you: approximate 12-month forecast by month, and whether legal prefers a simple MSA with an appended payment schedule or a signed PO. I can turn this into an initial quote + SOW for procurement.

Attaching: FastByte_RAMP_Schedule_v3.xlsx (ramp + credits table).

If this looks directionally right I’ll loop in Ben for pricing sanity checks and Vivek for approval on any nonstandard earn-back mechanics.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: FW: FastByte prepay proposal — pricing check

Vivek / Ben — forwarding Zoe's ask and my initial structure above. A couple of items I need quick input on:
1) Is the 18% term discount + $40k credits (upfront) within our starter-commit guardrails for Series A startups?
2) Earn-back credits tied to 15% MoM growth — nonstandard but helps protect Lighthouse in case they undershoot. Is this acceptable from a revenue recognition and credit liability standpoint?
3) If procurement insists on PO-based billing we might need to shift payment terms to net30 for the PO portion; any redlines risk here?

Numbers: base prepay $120k, credits $40k, earn-back pool $15k. Net effective commitment if all credits used ~ $65k net consumed (approx).

Can you both take a look and we’ll aim to respond by EOD Friday to respect Zoe’s timeline.

— H

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: FastByte prepay proposal — pricing check

Hannah — quick thoughts:
- 18% term discount on a 12mo $120k is within the Seed/Series A handbook for our competitive motion. Approve from pricing side.
- Earn-back mechanics: Finance will treat the earn-back as a refundable credit liability until it vests; $15k max is small enough to absorb. We should spell out clear vesting triggers and a max vesting cadence (e.g., up to 6 months).
- PO/net30: okay, but recommend we keep 50% upfront to avoid cash exposure if procurement pushes long payment windows. If FastByte is stubborn we can accept net30 for the PO portion only with a small surcharge (1.5%) to cover financing.

I'll draft a simple clause for the earn-back schedule and the partial net30 option; ping me if you want me to include the surcharge language.

— Ben

From: Zoe Park <procurement@fastbyte.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FastByte prepay bridge: proposal for credit vesting & ramp minimums

Hannah — thanks for the quick turnaround and the spreadsheet. Procurement reviewed and attached a couple of minor redlines (see Draft_SLA_Redlines.pdf). Two clarifications before we move to PO:
1) Can you confirm the credit expiry mechanics — we want unused front-loaded credits to roll into the extension window if we elect the top-up.
2) For the earn-back, procurement prefers vesting based on absolute usage thresholds (e.g., >= $12k monthly spend) rather than percentage growth, because % growth can be noisy for early-stage startups.

We’re good to proceed if Redwood can: allow credits to roll into the extension if we top-up within 30 days post-term; and change the earn-back trigger to the absolute monthly usage threshold (FastByte will provide a projected monthly baseline by EOD Tuesday).

If both are acceptable we’ll issue a PO next week.

— Zoe
